optionReasons.saa-med-184:option:1: Exclude from S3 and relying on local tapes abandons managed durability and creates regulatory risk — complete regression.
optionReasons.saa-med-184:option:2: Transfer Acceleration accelerates uploads — has no effect on storage cost.
optionReasons.saa-med-184:option:3: It's the closest because it keeps everything in Standard. PRESERVA the required retention and durability — the design works. But reverses the cost: the Standard is the most CARA for cold data; with ~zero access after 30 days and 12h of acceptable waiting, the Glacier cuts the cost in ~80-95%.

finalJustifications: Because lifecycle transitions records to Glacier (or Deep Archive) after the 30 hot days: equal durability, recovery in 12h acceptable and minimum cost per 10 years.
Because the lifecycle compresses the records in the transition to the Glacier, and the size reduction responds for most of the economy.
Because the lifecycle moves the records to a cheaper region after 30 days, keeping the Standard class at reduced regional rate.
Because the lifecycle freezes objects in read-only mode, and the S3 discount the cost of writing the monthly storage fee.

optionReasons.saa-med-185:option:0: One Zone-IA reduces durability (one AZ) and collects recovery — terrible for files that can suddenly become popular.
optionReasons.saa-med-185:option:1: The CloudFront accelerates the ENTREGA via cache — does not change the class or the cost of storing objects in the pocket.
optionReasons.saa-med-185:option:2: It's the closest because lifecycle is the classic optimization tool — but it's rule FIXA by age: the old files that saw success would be stuck in AI paying recovery rate at each access; unpredictable pattern by OBJETO is the case of Intelligent-Tiering.

finalJustifications: Because Intelligent-Tiering monitors each object and moves it between levels according to USO REAL — without manual rules, without recovery rate and without impact on hot objects.
Because Intelligent-Tiering predicts with ML which files will viralize and promotes them to the frequent level before the peak accesses arrive.
Because Intelligent-Tiering replicates popular objects to edge locations, combining cost optimization with global delivery.
Because Intelligent-Tiering charges a single rate levelled by all objects, and the average comes out lower than any fixed class.

optionReasons.saa-med-186:option:0: Config rule signals binary compliance — does not recommend alternative rates or estimate economy.
optionReasons.saa-med-186:option:1: It's the closest because the Trusted Advisor REALMENTE has verification of underutilized instances — but not in the Basic plan (business/enterprise requires), and even there points underutilization without recommending the ideal type by ML; recommendations with estimated savings are the Compute Optimizer.
optionReasons.saa-med-186:option:3: Reducing everything to a blind level would just drop the instances that are correctly dimensioned — without analysis there is no rightsizing.

finalJustifications: Because Computer Optimizer analyzes with ML the actual usage history (CPU, network and memory with the agent) and recommends appropriate types by instance, with estimated savings.
Because Computer Optimizer automatically applies the recommendations during the maintenance window, resizing the entire fleet.
Because Computer Optimizer is based on the workload tags of the instances to infer the ideal sizing of each of them.
Because Computer Optimizer negotiates with AWS a discount proportional to the waste detected in the 50 fora analysed.

optionReasons.saa-med-188:option:0: Forum Store is ephemeral — unacceptable for database; and 'free' dies along with data on the first stop.
optionReasons.saa-med-188:option:1: It's the closest because the Io2 Block Express is in fact the natural successor of the Io1 — but in the direction of DESEMPENHO maximum, not cost: remains in the premium family of IOPS provisioned; equivalent performance with much lower cost for 5.000 IOPS moderate is gp3.
optionReasons.saa-med-188:option:2: Oversize gp2 to win IOPS is the classic waste that the gp3 came to eliminate — pays useless GB.

finalJustifications: Because the gp3 covers the 5.000 IOPS on leave (up to 16.000) providing IOPS and throughput apart from size — at a cost per GB and per IOPS much smaller than yo1.
Because the gp3 inherits the IOPS provided for in the migration, maintaining the performance contract without any additional conversion cost.
Because the gp3 uses the same NVMe infrastructure as the io2, and the lowest price comes from hardware squeezing among more AZ customers.
Because the gp3 folds performance automatically at the bank peaks, dispensed with the fixed provisioning that the i1 required.

optionReasons.saa-med-189:option:0: Transfer Acceleration accelerates external uploads via edge — does not change route or rate NAT.
optionReasons.saa-med-189:option:1: It's the closest because the Direct Connect is also 'private connection with the AWS' — But turn on a datacenter ON-PREMISES to the cloud: for traffic of a sub-network of its own VPC to S3 it doesn't even apply; the costless internal route is the Gateway VPC Endpoint.
optionReasons.saa-med-189:option:2: Multiply NAT Gateways divides the same traffic at the same rate per GB — equal or higher cost, never lower.

finalJustifications: Because the Gateway Endpoint routes the traffic S3 by the internal network of the AWS without processing cost — monthly TB paying the rate of NAT travel for free.
Because Gateway Endpoint compresses data on the way to the S3, reducing the GB processed at the remaining rate of NAT.
Because the Gateway Endpoint applies a fixed monthly rate instead of the charge per GB, predictable for the volume of several TB of the application.
Because the Gateway Endpoint hides objects read frequently in VPC, and the hits eliminate the read traffic charged by the outside.

optionReasons.saa-med-190:option:0: Request Country is valid for accesses authenticated by other accounts AWS — anonymous visitors to a site can't even afford.
optionReasons.saa-med-190:option:1: Courts EC2 to serve static ADICIONAM cost of computing without reducing a transfer byte.
optionReasons.saa-med-190:option:2: It's the closest because the Global Accelerator also uses the global network and the edge of the AWS — but SEM cache: each repeated download would continue to exit the pocket and pay for the transfer; requisitions and repeated output cut is the cache of the CloudFront.

finalJustifications: Because CloudFront caches popular content in the edges: repeated downloads leave the cache (without touching the S3) and the remaining transfer pays the lower rates of CDN.
Because CloudFront transfers the output charge to the distribution, which has free monthly franchise of several traffic TBs.
Because CloudFront compresses the images and videos on the edge, and the reduction of bytes is the origin of all the economy observed in the invoice.
Because CloudFront limits repeated downloads of the same visitor, blocking the transfer waste of the original bucket.

optionReasons.saa-med-193:option:1: Spot for interactive development environments risk interruptions in the middle of the file — economics with direct side effect in the team.
optionReasons.saa-med-193:option:2: It's the closest because the RI of 1 year would give real discount (~40%) — but pays the 168 hours of the week to use ~55: the short automatic shutdown ~75% of the cost, much more than the discount of the reservation; schedule stop/start wins for use in commercial time.
optionReasons.saa-med-193:option:3: Depending on someone remembering every day is the manual process that you want to eliminate — and fails on the first holiday.

finalJustifications: Because stopping the instances outside of the time zeros the computer charge (does only the EBS): o EventBridge Scheduler with Lambda (or the Scheduler Forum) automates the stop and start.
Because the schedule hibernates the instances preserving the memory, and the team resumes the work exactly where it stopped the previous afternoon.
Because EventBridge negotiated reduced night rate for standing bodies, charged only for total inactivity time.
Because the Scheduler Forum converts t3.large to Spot out of the file, returning to On-Demand the next morning automatically.

optionReasons.saa-med-195:option:1: The CloudWatch has no 'last access per object' metric — the S3 are aggregated by pocket/filter.
optionReasons.saa-med-195:option:3: It's the closest because Intelligent-Tiering would also solve the underlying problem (optimize without manual rules) — but responds OUTRA question: the requirement is to get RECOMMENDATIONS for real data to decide the rules of Lifecycle; this prefix analysis is the Storage Class Analysis.

finalJustifications: Because Storage Class Analysis observes real accesses by prefix by 30+ days and recommends candidates to Standard-IA — the database to create rules.
Because Storage Class Analysis generates Lifecycle rules automatically from analysis, applying transitions without revision.
Because Storage Class Analysis marks each object with the expected cooling date, and Lifecycle reads that tag in transitions.
Because the Storage Class Analysis simulates the cost of each class over the history and migrates the prefixes with the highest estimated economy.
